title: Best tracker out there
body:
Hands down one of the best habit trackers that I’ve found out there. The user interface is very intuitive and easy to use. It has absolutely everything I was looking for.
1. Ability to set daily, weekly or monthly goals.
2. Ability to create a goal that requires multiple completions to count toward a streak (i.e. taking meds—you can create two instances that go toward one goal).
3. Reminders that you can create to help you remember to complete your goal. Let’s face it some of us get busy and lose track of things we want to do during the day and this helps immensely.

These functions are in the pro version which is completely worth it, without a doubt.

title: Almost perfect - Few updates needed
body: I first downloaded HabitKit in the ending of March 2025. I bought the lifetime premium version. When I first downloaded the app, it didn't have an option for putting your own emojis for habits, which was really frustrating. I'm very happy that they finally put an emoji update. I was tired of using a dog bone for my seafood habit. My issue with the new update is that you can't change the skin color of the emojis. It's also disappointing that you can't choose a set of Crayola like colors for your habits including brown, instead of the preset pastel colors that is given. No true red or solid purples just a pastel palette for everything... I also think that the counter for 1, 5, 10 , 15 shouldn't be there. I think that instead the only option should be to set your own number of "Pages read" for each habit. It would look much better for the eyes that way. Or at least give the option to turn it off and only have your own preset number. I also think that the HabitKit wrapped should be worded better and upgraded. Besides those things, this is a decent app for habit tracking. I do also believe having a bad habit tracker section or page would be great, and helpful for separation of good and bad habits. Plus not being able to sync to iCloud is hella wack. I can only give 2 stars because I know it could be better.

title: The Perfect App For What I Needed
body:
This app on my phone has been insanely helpful and so easy to use. I can track anything going on in my life and then easily look back over the history of my habit. Things like how frequently I’m vacuuming or if I took my medication each day or week. Every time I login and track my habits it also reminds me of things I might not have done yet like…oh I haven’t done that thing yet today. So I often get up to start or finish something because I see that it isn’t checked off for the day. 

What makes this app better than others I was looking at is that I’m 100% choosing my own categories and specific tasks. So my weird and wonderful lists are tailored perfectly to me, and there isn’t anything extraneous. 

The only complaint I have is that the data is only on your device. So I can see and use it on my phone but I can’t pull it up on my tablet or computer. I reached out to the developers and they say they hope to change this in the future. So fingers crossed, this app could get even better.

title: Simple is Beautiful
body:
This app checks a few boxes for me:
It allows me to see the trends of my habits over time; allowing me to see what i need to improve or fix. 
I can easily keep track of habits in multiple areas of my life, from working out, studying, and down to simple things like remembering to water my plants. 

While I can use notes, or a to-do list, or alarms, HabitKit allows you to come to one place for all of that-in a more fun and satisfying place. 

Honestly, the colors, icons, calendar, and organization through putting habits in certain categories keeps everything neat and aesthetically pleasingly. Everyone has their way of doing what this app does, but the way habit kit does it is what allows me to use it this thoroughly. Actually, it makes keeping in touch with my goals and to-dos fun-something lacking from other apps whether pre-installed, or otherwise. 

Being able to see your goals and habits stack up or lack over time is the big indicator on how well/poor Im doing, and thats the motivator for however you choose to track your trends. 

Long time user of the app, and I’ll keep on using it to perfect my routine. Well done Habitkit, looking forward to future updates that reflect the simple brilliance you have here already.

title: A Game Changer
body:
I recently turned started using a minimalist phone setup to help me to be more productive. A key part of the design was adding HabitKit widgets to my home screen. It's very motivating to see your habit history packed into a beautiful little chart, with the ability to check off (or increment) habits without having to open the app. After making these changes to my phone, this past week has been the most productive week of my life, and I sincerely believe HabitKit has been the main reason for that. 

The support is also incredible. I reached out to the solo developer via email, asking him about 2 different features I was hoping he could add to the app. 2 days later, he got back to me, in a very friendly and well-thought-out email. In this email, he told me that he had already been working on adding the first feature, and the other had been added to his todo list. Given that he is a solo developer, and also working on another up-and-coming app at the same time, I'd say his support services are the best I've ever seen, from any app on the app store.

title: One of the best habit tracking apps - but NEEDS iOS Reminders integration and maybe APIs exposed ?
body:
This is by far the most visually appealing app. I was actually going to develop my own app which was similar to this, where it had the altair heatmap chart. But this goes beyond my initial idea and also has step counts/tiered counting. Moreover, the ease of completing a task with a tap, setting of reminders, color coding and the availability to switch between three different views is exactly what I needed.

This is way better than todoist, it is simple and intuitive. Most other apps have a lot of clutter and have too many details and clunky interfaces.

One important feature that is missing though is its integration with Calendar and Reminders. Not just that, PLEASE expose APIs to interact with the data, this would have a limited use case, but still could be very useful. For example, one could ingest their daily step count and automatically mark a habit. Another example is that say if I want to block a particular app unless I do X, it could allow it to do so. Lets say that I have a habit like “no scrolling videos in the morning for 2 hours”, I should be able to enforce this and mark the habit only when certain conditions outside the app are met - I know this is a little outside the scope of this app and probably would fit into another “habit enforcer” app that could integrate with this, but in any case this requires REST APIs to be exposed. I would love to partner with the dev and work on this idea.

title: Simple, Effective, and Visually Elegant
body:
UPDATE (2025-02-05)

Not sure how long I’ve been using HabitKit (just checked and it has been a bit over two years) and I’m still loving it ♥️

It’s simple, has the features I want, and zero bloat. I love that you can enable/disable streaks because I’m no longer doing streaked habits.

I’ve been using it as a widget stack on my Home Screen (small size, all habits in the stack) and it’s just perfect like this!

—=•=— 

I’ve been using the “don’t break the chain” method of habit building for about a billion years. I’ve used apps and my own paper trackers. They all work, more or less, but some just feel better than others, and with something simple like habit tracking, feel is 90% of what’s important.

HabitKit has FEEL son!

There’s something about the simplicity of the app and the ease of logging that just feels right. But more than that, the visual display of your streak is the best I’ve come across. It’s RIGHT in your face. There’s no ignoring it… and that’s a very very good thing.

author: Verhoffs

title: Almost perfect
body:
I’ve tried a few habit apps, and absolutely love using this one so far. The user experience is extremely intuitive and easy to use, and has (almost) all the features I was looking for. Just as an example, the Shortcuts integration is great for me - I was able to integrate HabitKit into an existing Shortcut I was using for recording a daily journal, and so now recording one will also automatically mark the habit complete for the day too. The widgets are really nice too and improve the overall interaction.

All that said, there are just a few additional features I’d like to see. First, a MacOS version of the app would be great, though I can confirm that it does work to install the iOS version. However, it would really be awesome if it could sync to iCloud both to make this actually usable, as well as to make it easy when you get a new device. There is an export / import feature for this but this would make it a lot. Lee seamless. Finally, it would be nice to have additional Shortcuts support - the ability to look at past completions / streaks, change completion for other dates, export / import from Shortcut, etc.

With that list, why did I still give it 5 stars? Because even as-is it is incredibly useful and I would recommend it to everyone even without these features (though they would be great!)

title: Solid and simple
body:
I love an app that does exactly what it says on the tin. Works well with shortcuts for automation. Happy to purchase the lifetime pro license. Data seems local so works great no matter your network conditions and you never see a loading spinner 

Feature requests: 

- support CloudKit for syncing across devices. 
- Deep links for specific habits or filters
- add a simple small one click tracking widget. The current widgets should open the selected habit instead of the dashboard too 

If you find NFC tags fussy for habit tracking, flic buttons work alright if you have pushcut + an automation server (use the web request action to trigger your habit tracking shortcut). 

It’d be great if there was a way to support habit tracking actions in home automations (not just personal automations) to avoid this whole song and dance. 

Overall, great application, would recommend to a friend

title: 10/10 Customer Satisfaction
body:
If you’re looking to change your life, “atomic habits” style, then you need this app. Not the other habit trackers.. you need this one. This one right here is the best. 

I honestly can’t remember what the free version is like because I saw the value of upgrading within a week of downloading.

I’ve added HabitKit widgets all across my phone and not only have I see my productivity increase, but my lifestyle and mindset have greatly benefited from using this app. 

If Apple were to release a habit tracking app, it wouldn’t compare to this one. It’s sleek, easily customizable, and it’s just an overall better application compared to other habit trackers on the App Store.

If you’re NOT a fan of subscription based services, then THIS IS THE APP FOR YOU. I made a one time payment and this developer has continued to push out updates with an increasing attention to detail. The developer has helped me troubleshoot and they might even incorporate some of my feedback within future updates. 

If you’re hesitant to buy their product, then think of it this way. Apple wants you to subscribe to their iCloud service indefinitely and the developer of this app only wants a one-time contribution from you. That’s it. You’re not renting this product, it is yours to keep. You receive all the future benefits without a monthly/yearly recurring charge to your bank.

title: Great Simple App, Great Developer, Some Limitations
body:
I really love how simple and easy this app is to use. The pricing is also extremely reasonable for $0.99 when most apps charge way more just for some basic functions. I think it would be great if we would were able to create our own account so we can sync progress across different devices. 

I have ADHD and this app really helps me stay motivated and manage my executive dysfunction because I have to gamify EVERYTHING just to do simple things. I like how we are able to select different days for when we want to track a habit, but I wish we could select different reminder times for different days as well under the same habit. Say you want to add a yoga habit for each day, but want reminders at 2:00pm on certain days and 3:00pm on other days for those with varying schedules.

 I also think sub-habit/task would be an interesting game changer. Say you’re trying to incorporate an entire morning routine habit, you can just label the habit morning routine, and you can click it to open, add a sub-habit/task, like make bed, brush teeth, do skin care, and once you check off all three of those things, it will complete that habit for the day. I feel like this would help with lessening the amount of habits you have to make when one habit can incorporate many things you want to do!

title: Fantastic Habit Tracker from a Responsive Developer
body:
The app is an intuitive, visually pleasing way to track your habits. It does a great job of allowing users to customize their habits while not crowding the ui or creating a convoluted user experience. Overall, it is a near-perfect habit tracker with a nice minimalist aesthetic

Also, the developer shows a lot of respect for the users of the app. I wrote to them regarding some functionality that I was hoping they would add and they quickly wrote back to let me know they were working on that. A couple months later they reached out to let me know they were rolling out that feature! In my experience, it is hard to find a developer that is so genuinely responsive to user feedback

Lastly, the app, which does have a premium option, makes the non-premium version actually worthwhile to use and offers the premium version via both subscription and one-time-purchase. Both of those are big pluses in my book!

author: Mr Kreus

title: An excellent habit tracker
body:
I love the simple design and color scheme. It works very well for me as a habit tracker.

I have two gripes at the moment. The first is this: I wish you could tap on the check-mark in the home screen widget at it would just mark the habit as complete, instead of opening up the app for you to mark it yourself. I don’t know if this is an iPhone limitation, or user error, or what, but it would be nice

The second is that it costs money. I think it’s a reasonable enough price to pay, but it’s a little shady that you market the app as free, when the features that make it useful are locked behind a paywall. Just sell the app for that amount on the App Store. Or better yet, let it be free. I don’t see what costs you are incurring providing this excellent service to your fellow men.

That being said, I paid for it, and so far it has been worth the cost.

title: Effective and Motivating Habit Tracker!
body:
As someone who has always struggled with maintaining consistency in my daily habits, I have tried numerous habit tracking apps in the past. However, none of them have managed to motivate and engage me as much as HabitKit! This app has completely transformed my approach to habit tracking and has helped me build lasting habits that I can finally stick to.

The daily notifications are a gentle but effective reminder to complete my habits, making it nearly impossible to forget or procrastinate. The best part, though, is the GitHub contribution-style chart that visually represents my progress. This brilliant feature has turned habit tracking into an exciting game, where I eagerly work to maintain my streak and fill in the chart.

The interface is clean, intuitive, and user-friendly, allowing me to easily add, edit, and manage my habits. The customization options are also impressive, enabling me to tailor the notifications and chart according to my preferences.

HabitKit has not only helped me stay consistent in my daily routines but has also significantly improved my productivity and overall well-being. I am genuinely grateful for this app and highly recommend it to anyone looking to build and maintain healthy habits. Give HabitKit a try, and I promise you won't be disappointed!

title: The Ultimate Habit Tracking App!
body:
I absolutely love HabitKit! It is by far the best habit tracking app I have ever used. The tile-based grid charts make it super easy to visualize my progress, and the customization options for the dashboard are a great touch. The ability to choose my own colors, icons, and descriptions really helps me to personalize the app to my own needs and goals.

One of the things I love most about HabitKit is the motivation it provides. Seeing the tiles on my dashboard fill up with color as I complete my habits is a great way to stay motivated and on track. The app is also very user-friendly and easy to navigate. I highly recommend HabitKit to anyone looking to form new habits or break old ones.

Overall, I would give HabitKit a solid 5 out of 5 stars. It has truly made a difference in my life and I am so grateful to have found it. Thank you, Sebastian, for creating such a wonderful app!
